newsitem.title: UK: Wm. Morrison warns sales growth could slow.
newsitem.headline: Wm. Morrison warns sales growth could slow.

text.p: British food retailer William Morrison Supermarkets Plc warned on Thursday that, because of fierce competition, sales growth in the second half of the year was unlikely to match that of the first six months.

"During the second half of the year we expect trading conditions to remain difficult and sales are unlikely to maintain the growth seen in the first six months," the company said in its results statement.
In the six weeks since the end of its half-year, supermarket takings, including value added tax, had risen by 5.6 percent, or 0.7 percent excluding stores opened since January 1995, it said.
Petrol sales, under fire from a petrol price war led by oil giants such as Exxon Corp's Esso unit, fell 6.1 percent on a like-for-like basis, while other products saw sales rise.
Excluding petrol sales, total sales in the six weeks were 6.1 percent higher, or 1.3 percent on a like-for-like basis.

The firm, which earlier posted an eight percent rise in first-half pretax profits to 55.2 million stg on sales that breached one billion stg for the first time, said trading conditions had been "some of the most demanding for many years".

"It is the first time in 20 years that the company has no new store openings and with ever increasing competitor activity, the petrol price war and the BSE scare (mad cow disease) the group has performed well to produce an increase in turnover of 9.3 percent," it said.

Supermarket takings excluding petrol were 11.6 percent ahead and 3.1 percent ahead in existing stores, which the company said was "extremely encouraging" when allowing for disruption to trade caused by a store refurbishment programme.
"The directors believe the benefits of recent substantial investment will continue to accrue and the prospects for the group remain encouraging," the company said.
